title: Customer tier mapping notes (Unit Economics dashboard)
text:
Context
- For the internal Unit Economics dashboard we need a stable, finance-aligned “customer_tier” dimension to support drilldowns and blended $/1M output tokens.
- Customer tier is NOT equivalent to “plan” in all cases (Dedicated/Private are often contract + routing reality, not purely billing sku).
- Goal: deterministic mapping that can be applied consistently in:
  (a) runtime/gateway token metering events (near-real-time)
  (b) hourly aggregation job (warehouse)
  (c) reconciliation reports vs billing

Current working tier taxonomy (v1)
- self_serve
- enterprise
- dedicated
- private

Notes:
- “enterprise” here means: hosted/shared infra but sold via contract (SLA, invoicing, negotiated pricing). Not “Dedicated” or “Private”.
- Dedicated/Private should win over enterprise if both are true (common: enterprise customer also has dedicated pools).

Proposed precedence (highest to lowest)
1) private
2) dedicated
3) enterprise
4) self_serve

Rationale: deployment mode is the clearest indicator of cost structure + attribution assumptions (idle, reserved capacity, etc.).

Signals we can use (and where they live)
1) Billing plan / subscription
- Source: Billing system (Stripe for self-serve; invoicing platform for enterprise), plus internal “plans” table.
- Useful fields:
  - billing_account_id
  - plan_slug (e.g., hosted_free, hosted_pro, hosted_enterprise)
  - is_invoiced (boolean)
  - committed_spend_usd (nullable)
  - start_at/end_at
- Pros: authoritative for self_serve vs enterprise split.
- Cons: Dedicated/Private may not show up as a plan slug consistently (or only as add-on SKUs).

2) Contract / deal flags
- Source: Contracts metadata service (sync from Sales ops). Some fields are in CRM (HubSpot/Salesforce equivalents) but we should NOT rely on CRM directly in pipeline.
- Useful fields:
  - contract_type: msa | order_form | none
  - deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private
  - has_sla: true/false
  - data_residency_required: true/false
  - invoice_terms: net30/net45
- Pros: best source for Dedicated/Private intent; finance expects contract metadata to define enterprise cohorts.
- Cons: lag / backfill (contract updates happen manually); edge cases during migration.

3) Routing / infrastructure reality
- Source: Gateway/routing config + infra tags (which request went to which capacity pool)
- Useful fields:
  - capacity_type: shared | dedicated_pool | private_cluster
  - pool_id / cluster_id
  - org_id / project_id
- Pros: closest to truth for where tokens were served; good for “what actually happened” attribution.
- Cons: not ideal as the single source-of-truth for “tier” because customers can occasionally burst to shared, run mixed mode, or have misrouted traffic.

What “authoritative source” should be?
Recommendation: a single internal “Customer Entitlements” service/table that is the authoritative tier classifier, computed from Billing + Contracts, and optionally validated against routing.
- Name (proposal): customer_tier_snapshot
- Owned by: Platform Eng (inputs owned by Finance Ops + Sales Ops + Telemetry)
- Update cadence:
  - daily full snapshot + change-data-capture when possible
  - tier computed with effective_start/end times (at least day-level; hourly would be nice but probably overkill for v1)
- Consumption:
  - Telemetry ingestion joins tier snapshot by org_id/customer_id + request timestamp
  - Aggregation job uses already-attributed tier on events; reconciliation can re-join to debug

Tier definitions (operational)
Self-serve
- Definition: customer pays via self-serve plan (card), no contract flags indicating enterprise, and not on dedicated/private capacity.
- Primary signal: billing plan slug in {hosted_free, hosted_pro, ...} AND is_invoiced=false AND no active contract_type.
- Notes:
  - Free credits still count as self_serve (unless issued under enterprise pilot; see edge cases).

Enterprise
- Definition: hosted/shared infra but sold/managed via contract/invoice (includes negotiated discounts).
- Primary signal: is_invoiced=true OR active contract_type != none, AND deployment_mode=hosted.
- Secondary signal: “enterprise_support” entitlement flag.

Dedicated
- Definition: traffic served on a dedicated GPU pool reserved for that customer (or logically isolated capacity) under a contract.
- Primary signal: contract deployment_mode=dedicated OR entitlement has_dedicated=true.
- Validation signal: routing capacity_type=dedicated_pool for >= X% of tokens in a lookback window.
- Note: we need to decide what happens when a Dedicated customer bursts/falls back to shared due to capacity issues.
  - Proposal: tier remains dedicated (customer-level tier), but we keep capacity_type as a separate dimension for cost attribution and explaining anomalies.

Private
- Definition: traffic served in customer VPC/on-prem/private control plane.
- Primary signal: contract deployment_mode=private OR entitlement has_private=true.
- Validation signal: routing capacity_type=private_cluster.

Implementation proposal (v1)
- Emit BOTH:
  - customer_tier (computed, stable)
  - capacity_type (observed at request routing)
- In the dashboard, default drilldown is customer_tier; capacity_type is a secondary filter/drilldown (optional for v1 UI but should be in the warehouse view).

Edge cases to handle (capture explicitly so we don’t silently misclassify)
1) Mixed-mode customers (common in enterprise)
- Example: enterprise hosted + dedicated pool for one workload.
- If we only have customer-level tier, we lose nuance.
- Proposed handling:
  - customer_tier = dedicated (wins)
  - capacity_type captures shared vs dedicated per request
  - In top-N tables, show a warning if customer_tier != capacity_type majority (diagnostic)

2) Private customers with hosted sandbox / evaluation
- Some Private deals start with hosted pilot.
- Proposed: tier is time-bounded.
  - Before private effective_start: enterprise (hosted) or self_serve depending on billing.
  - After: private.

3) Pilot credits / “enterprise trial”
- Sales sometimes issues credits but customer is considered enterprise cohort.
- We need a flag like sales_motion = enterprise_pilot.
- Proposal: treat as enterprise if active contract exists OR explicit enterprise_pilot flag is true.

4) Resellers / channel partners
- Org IDs may represent partner accounts serving end customers.
- For unit economics we care about cost vs our revenue; tier should reflect our contract.
- Proposal:
  - tier based on our billing entity (partner) not end-customer.
  - Do NOT attempt to derive end-customer tier v1.
  - Ensure we don’t leak end-customer identifiers into drilldowns.

5) Internal / dogfood / test orgs
- Need to exclude or mark separately to avoid skew.
- Proposal: customer_tier = internal (NOT in v1 taxonomy?) OR tag org as is_internal=true and exclude in default views.
- If we can’t add a new tier, we should at least provide is_internal dimension.

6) Credits-only / free users
- Some “self_serve” orgs only generate cost, no revenue.
- Tier is still self_serve; revenue cohort handled elsewhere.
- But we should be able to filter out “free_only” for finance views.

7) Customer migrations (plan changes, contract upgrades)
- Need effective dating and reproducibility.
- Finance request: ability to reproduce last quarter numbers even if tier changed mid-quarter.
- Proposal:
  - tier snapshot keyed by (org_id, effective_start, effective_end)
  - pipeline uses request timestamp to join
  - store tier_version (mapping rules version) so we can audit changes

8) Multiple orgs under one billing account
- Some enterprise customers have multiple org_ids/projects.
- Tier should be consistent across all under billing_account_id unless explicitly overridden.
- Proposal: mapping table supports both org_id-level overrides and billing_account-level default.

9) Dedicated capacity shared across multiple customers (rare but happens in early programs)
- If a pool_id is shared, routing-based inference could mislead.
- Need a pool_id -> billing_account_id mapping maintained by Infra.

10) “Enterprise” flag drift between systems
- Billing says invoiced, contract metadata missing (or vice versa).
- In conflicts, what wins?
  - Proposal: Contracts/Deal system wins for enterprise/dedicated/private intent; billing wins for self_serve vs invoiced when no contract exists.
  - Log conflicts to a weekly report.

Data model sketch (no schema nesting here, just notes)
- customer_tier_snapshot columns (proposal)
  - org_id
  - billing_account_id
  - customer_name (optional, internal only)
  - customer_tier (self_serve|enterprise|dedicated|private)
  - effective_start_at
  - effective_end_at
  - source_billing_plan_slug
  - source_is_invoiced
  - source_contract_deployment_mode
  - source_entitlement_flags (flattened booleans: has_dedicated, has_private, enterprise_pilot)
  - mapping_rule_version
  - updated_at

Telemetry implications
- We should avoid joining to billing/contract systems in the hot path at request time.
- Preferred:
  - Tier join at ingestion time (stream processor / ETL) using the snapshot table.
  - For real-time metrics, allow a short lag (minutes) and accept that newly-created orgs default to self_serve until snapshot catches up.
- Requirement: deterministic tier for every metering event (no nulls).
  - If join fails: set customer_tier=unknown and alert; but for dashboard v1 we should try hard to keep unknown <0.1%.

Backfill plan
- Need a backfill job to re-attribute tier historically once snapshot is available.
- Note: tier can change over time, so backfill must use timestamp join (not “latest tier”).

Validation / sanity checks
- Daily:
  - count(org_id) by tier; look for sudden movements
  - % events with unknown tier
  - Dedicated/Private customers whose capacity_type is mostly shared (might indicate misrouting)
- Weekly:
  - spot-check top 20 spend orgs vs finance list
  - reconcile enterprise cohort size vs invoiced accounts

Open questions
1) Do we need an explicit “internal” tier, or is is_internal boolean enough for v1?
2) For Dedicated customers that temporarily fall back to shared (capacity crunch):
   - should those tokens be attributed to dedicated tier or enterprise tier? (Finance preference seems “dedicated tier”, but cost attribution will be different.)
3) Source-of-truth system name/ownership: do we implement in Platform Eng DB, or ask Data Eng to host in warehouse as a governed dimension?
4) How do we handle org_id splits/merges (rare but does happen during enterprise onboarding)?

Action items (as of 2025-02-04)
- [Logan/Nadia] confirm telemetry pipeline join location + freshness expectations (ties into SLO doc)
- [Rishi/Laura] provide definitive rules for enterprise_pilot + invoiced edge cases for FP&A reporting
- [Cole/Mei] prototype customer_tier_snapshot table in warehouse + example join query for hourly aggregation
- [Chloe/Jada] confirm API and UI terminology (“enterprise” vs “contracted hosted”) to avoid confusion

Quick examples (for alignment)
- Org A: Stripe plan=hosted_pro, no contract -> self_serve
- Org B: invoiced=true, deployment_mode=hosted -> enterprise
- Org C: contract says dedicated, routing is 80% dedicated_pool + 20% shared -> customer_tier=dedicated, capacity_type explains the 20%
- Org D: contract says private starting Feb 15; before Feb 15 invoiced hosted -> enterprise until Feb 14, then private on/after Feb 15
